title: Fennel and the Big Purple Frustrated
subtitle: A story about feeling frustrated
story: Fennel wanted to tie his shoes
all by himself — there was nothing to lose!
top
He made a loop. He made a twirl.
The laces just flopped in a floppy swirl.
top
He pulled and he pulled. It came out a mess.
He tried once more. And once more. No success.
top
A purple coil popped out of his chest.
It wound itself tight. It would not rest.
top
Tighter and tighter, the coil went round.
“I can’t! I can’t!” he said with a frown.
top
He tossed down his shoe. It flew through the air.
Papa Bear came and sat on the stair.
top
“Frustrated is hard,” said Papa. “I know.
Big things take time. We can take it slow.”
top
“First, PAUSE. Put your shoe down and shake.
Shake out your paws, for goodness’ sake!”
top
“Next, TRY a new way. Make bunny ears two.
Cross them and tuck them. See what you can do.”
top
“Last, ASK for a hand. It’s not giving in.
A helping paw is a place to begin.”
top
Loop, swoop, pull — and the knot held tight!
The purple coil faded from sight.
top
Now when the purple gets tight and tough,
Fennel knows: Pause. Try. Ask. That’s enough!
top
steps: Stop. Put it down. Shake out your paws.
Ask for a hand or a hint.
note_lines: Wait before helping. Let your child pause first.
Show a new way instead of doing it for them.

listing.description:
Fennel wants to tie his shoes all by himself. But the laces flop, the loops slip, and a tight purple coil pops out of his chest.

The Big Purple Frustrated winds tighter and tighter with every try, until Papa Bear sits down beside him and shows him a better way.

With three patient steps — Pause. Try. Ask. — little readers learn that frustrated is okay, and that hard things get easier with practice and help.

Inside this warm rhyming picture book:

  • A cozy read-aloud rhyme for ages 3–6, perfect for kids learning new skills
  • A kid-friendly image of frustration as a coiled purple spring that unwinds
  • Three easy steps children can copy: Pause, Try, Ask
  • A note for grown-ups with simple ways to coach through frustration
  • Soft watercolor-style illustrations

Book 8 in the Fennel's Feelings series. A gentle story about tying shoes, trying again, and asking for help.
